BLOCK - round 1, exact head 916de5628b586eee641053915de5227806c5e050.

R315-F001 (P2, cost/core scope): the non-dry reaper still materializes the entire roster every sweep.

crates/daemon/src/reaper.rs:268-274 computes receipt.after with registry.list(SeatFilter::default()), then discards tombstoned descriptors in Rust. death_sweep::sweep always calls this with dry_run=false (crates/daemon/src/death_sweep.rs:90-98), including ticks that reap nothing. Thus the automatic 5-second loop still performs one full LIST_SQL scan and decodes every historical seat per tick. The supplied 6.26 -> 0.34 ms timing measures only the initial list, not both reads in a sweep. The PR's reaper scaling claim is therefore incomplete: the final count remains O(all historical seats), not O(live seats).

Fix in this PR's round 2, not a new hardening project: fetch live_only again for receipt.after and take that vector's length, just as the initial count does. Keep the final fresh read; do not replace it with before-minus-reaped arithmetic, which would lose concurrent registration/tombstone effects. Correct the cost row and qualify the timing as a per-list measurement. A focused recording-registry regression that rejects an unfiltered list on either read would defend the actual consumer, rather than only an exported query constant. This is the same recurring F258 read and a small completion of the stated optimization.

Other requested checks pass:

- Reaper behavior: the initial SQL restriction is equivalent to the previous Rust restriction for valid registry rows. Already tombstoned seats were never candidates or receipt entries. A row tombstoned between list and get is still skipped (reaper.rs:210-212); a row changed after get is still refused by the full-descriptor comparison under the write transaction (registry.rs:61-77). A revive omitted from an already-tombstoned snapshot waits until the next sweep exactly as before. Obituaries still come only from successful conditional tombstones, with their captured descriptors; parent retirement is separately checked by get. No new revival/retirement path or lost holding cleanup was introduced.
